title: feat(baseline): validate baseline entries against the current rule registry
problem: A baseline may reference rule ids that no longer exist or have been renamed, and the mismatch is silent.
why: Stale baselines quietly stop suppressing and can confuse reviewers.
scope: On load, compare recorded rule ids against the registry and emit diagnostics for unknown ids.
guidance: Keep forward compatibility: unknown ids warn, they do not fail.
tests: Unit and CLI tests with a stale baseline

title: feat(baseline): add a prune command for resolved entries
problem: Resolved findings linger in the baseline forever, inflating the file and hiding progress.
why: Pruning keeps baselines meaningful and reviewable.
scope: Add a command or flag that rewrites the baseline with only currently-present findings.
guidance: Require an explicit action; never prune as a side effect of scanning.
security: Record a diff summary so pruning is auditable.

title: feat(baseline): support merging multiple baseline files
problem: Monorepos may keep per-package baselines but cannot combine them for a single scan.
why: Merging allows team-owned baselines to compose.
scope: Accept multiple baseline files and merge by fingerprint with deterministic conflict handling.
guidance: Deduplicate identical fingerprints; keep the first severity encountered in sorted order.

title: feat(baseline): add a TOML baseline format option
problem: Baselines are JSON only, which is not diff-friendly for large reviewed files.
why: A TOML option can produce friendlier diffs in code review.
scope: Support reading and writing a TOML baseline with the same fields and a format marker.
guidance: Auto-detect format on read; keep JSON as the default.

title: fix(baseline): handle truncated and corrupted baseline files gracefully
problem: A partially written or corrupted baseline produces a parse error that may be hard to diagnose in CI.
why: Clear, safe handling prevents confusing failures and accidental gate bypass.
scope: Detect truncation, emit an actionable error with the file and position, and never treat it as empty.
guidance: Fail closed: a broken baseline must not silently suppress nothing or everything.
acceptance: Corruption produces a clear error and exit code 3
tests: Unit and CLI tests with truncated JSON
security: Fail-closed behavior is essential for trust.

title: feat(report): include baseline new/existing/resolved in JSON and SARIF
problem: Baseline comparison is printed to stderr but not represented in machine-readable reports.
why: CI dashboards and code scanning need structured baseline state.
scope: Add baseline summary counts and per-finding baseline status to JSON, and map status into SARIF properties.
guidance: Keep the fields additive and documented.

title: feat(cli): add git-based incremental scanning with --changed-since
problem: Changed-file scanning requires an external git invocation to produce a file list.
why: Built-in change detection simplifies CI and developer workflows.
scope: Add `--changed-since <ref>` that derives changed Rust files via git, or from a supplied file when git is unavailable.
guidance: Shell out to git read-only; if git is missing, fail with a clear message and document fallback.
tests: CLI test in a temporary git repository
security: Read-only git invocation; treat output as untrusted paths and validate them.

title: feat(baseline): offer path-independent fingerprints for renamed files
problem: Renaming or moving a file changes every fingerprint, so all findings appear new.
why: Refactors are common and should not reset a baseline.
scope: Add an opt-in fingerprint mode that omits the file path, with clear documentation of the trade-off.
guidance: Keep the current behavior as default; warn about collisions when omitting the path.
security: Omitting the path increases collision risk; document it explicitly.

title: docs(ci): document and test the fail-on-new-only CI policy matrix
problem: The relationship between `--baseline`, `--new-only`, and `--fail-on` is powerful but only briefly documented.
why: A policy matrix prevents misconfiguration that either blocks CI or lets regressions through.
scope: Add a table of combinations with expected exit behavior, and a test asserting each combination.
guidance: Base the table on real CLI tests.

title: perf(baseline): handle very large baselines efficiently
problem: Baseline comparison builds a fresh fingerprint set on each check and loads the whole file into memory.
why: Large repositories can accumulate thousands of accepted findings.
scope: Measure comparison cost at scale and optimize lookup to a single pass with a reusable set.
guidance: Add a benchmark fixture for a large baseline and document the measured cost.
acceptance: No regression and lookup is O(n)
security: Bound memory use for untrusted baseline files.
